correctness.rationale: The exact Floquet determinant of arXiv:2409.03538v1 was expanded through order k^5. The cubic coefficient reproduces the published low-energy expression up to an irrelevant overall sign. Uniformity follows because the determinant is a finite trigonometric polynomial on the compact Bloch torus. Away from the two critical scales the cubic coefficient has a strict uniform sign or changes sign, giving the gap/contact alternatives. At the lower and upper critical scales the fifth-order coefficient was simplified analytically and proved positive; the sign geometry then yields a lower endpoint with spectral contact and an upper endpoint without it. The multiplicative width inequalities reduce to exact elementary inequalities in reciprocal shape variables. The packaged verifier checks representative determinant signs but is not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The primary paper gives the exact determinant, the cubic low-energy expansion, and strict unequal-length conditions, but it does not settle the equality cases for general anisotropic cells, does not formulate the exact uniform-dilation phase interval, and does not prove the universal factor-two shape law. The same paper's equilateral special case resolves only one shape. The 2014/2015 dilated-honeycomb predecessor uses delta coupling, and the 2017/2018 preferred-orientation paper uses the original R coupling rather than the anisotropic negative-R model. Published-record searches found no statement implying the endpoint classification or the width optimum.
residual_risks: An unindexed note could have carried out the same fifth-order endpoint expansion under different terminology.

The 2025 journal version of the primary preprint could contain editorial changes; the accepted claim is independently derived from the publicly dated v1 determinant, so such changes would affect originality comparison rather than the proof unless the determinant itself changed.

value.rationale: Uniform dilation is the natural isotropic-strain path through the three edge-length parameters. The source leaves the general critical equalities unresolved even though its equilateral example shows that endpoint inclusion is nontrivial. Settling the exact half-closed interval identifies a genuine re-entrant gap/contact/gap phase diagram. The factor-two theorem then turns the interval into a shape invariant and proves that the equilateral cell is uniquely least robust, while reciprocal-nontriangle shapes have an even wider sqrt(5) minimum. This is structural spectral information, not a parameter renaming or numerical recomputation.
